findings.title: `float: right` on .small-action button is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container
findings.body: `.small-action` is turned into a flex container via `@include flexbox()`, which makes `.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc` and `button` flex items. The CSS Flexbox spec states that `float` has no effect on flex items, so the `float: right` left on `button` (and `float: left` on `.topic-avatar`) no longer does anything. Because `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1`/width and the button has no `margin-left: auto`, the action button (e.g. the close/archive toggle) will now render immediately after the description text instead of at the right edge of the row — a visible layout regression for every small-action post. The button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the desc needs `flex: 1`) to restore the right alignment.

findings.title: Right-alignment of .panel relies on `margin-left: auto`, which the legacy `-webkit-box` model emitted by the mixin does not honor
findings.body: The `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` for legacy WebKit/Gecko engines (Android stock browser < 4.4, Safari < 6.1, old Chrome). In the 2009 box model, auto margins are not used for distribution and `float` is ignored on box children, so with `float: right` removed and only `margin-left: auto` added, `.panel` (the icons/login buttons) will sit directly after the site title instead of at the right edge of the header on exactly the browsers the prefixes are meant to support. Either drop the legacy prefixes (and accept modern-flexbox-only), or add a legacy-compatible fallback such as `-webkit-box-flex: 1` on `.title`/`.extra-info-wrapper` or `-webkit-box-pack: justify` on `.contents`.

findings.title: Float-based header layout removed with no fallback for browsers without any flexbox support
findings.body: `.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }` were deleted and replaced solely by flexbox on `.contents`. Browsers with no flexbox implementation at all (IE9 and older, Opera Mini) will now render `.title`, `.extra-info-wrapper` and `.panel` as stacked block elements, breaking the header entirely rather than degrading. If any such browser is still in the support matrix the floats should be kept as a fallback (flexbox ignores floats on flex items, so keeping them is harmless for flex-capable browsers).

findings.title: .extra-info-wrapper as a flex item has `min-width: auto`, so long topic titles will push .panel out of the header
findings.body: Now that `.contents` is a flex container, `.extra-info-wrapper` (which holds the docked topic title and category badge) becomes a flex item. Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, meaning they refuse to shrink below their content's min-content width. The wrapper gets `order(2)` but no `flex: 1 1 auto` / `min-width: 0` / `overflow: hidden`, so a long topic title (especially one with `white-space: nowrap`, as applied to `.badge-wrapper`) will widen the item and push `.panel` outside the header or wrap the row, instead of truncating as the previous float layout allowed. Add `min-width: 0; flex: 1;` (with `overflow: hidden`/ellipsis as desired) to the wrapper.

findings.title: Removing paragraph margins in .custom-message collapses spacing between multi-paragraph messages
findings.body:
`.small-action .small-action-desc .custom-message p` had `margin: 5px 0` and now has `margin: 0`. Custom close/archive/pin messages can contain multiple paragraphs (the message is cooked markdown), so consecutive `

` elements will now render with no vertical separation and read as a single run-on block. If the intent was only to remove the outer top/bottom spacing for the flex centering, use `p + p { margin-top: 5px }` or zero only `:first-child`/`:last-child` margins.

findings.title: align-items mixin forwards the modern keyword unchanged to legacy prefixes and emits a non-existent `-ms-align-items` property
findings.body: `-webkit-box-align` (2009 model) and `-ms-flex-align` (IE10 2012 draft) accept `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`; the mixin passes `$alignment` through verbatim, so any future `@include align-items(flex-start)` silently produces invalid declarations for those engines (only `center`/`baseline`, the values used today, happen to coincide). Additionally `-ms-align-items` was never implemented by any IE version (IE11 uses unprefixed `align-items`), so that line is dead output in every compiled stylesheet. Either map the keywords inside the mixin or drop the legacy prefixes to avoid a mixin that looks portable but isn't. (Same class of issue in `order()`: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` is 1-based while `order` is 0-based, so identical values do not produce identical relative ordering against default items.)

findings.title: PR title claims a performance optimization; the change is a layout refactor and the description is a placeholder
findings.body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" but nothing in the diff affects rendering/scrolling performance — it swaps float positioning for flexbox and adds vendor-prefix mixins, which if anything emits more CSS. The description is just "Test 5". A maintainer reading the history will be misled about why the header, small-action and badge layouts changed; the title/description should describe the actual change (float → flexbox layout, vendor-prefix mixins) and note the visual changes (removed bullet margin, small-action spacing).
